newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money stable at 13.0/15.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money stable at 13.0/15.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money stabilised at 13.0/15.0 percent on Monday morning after jumping to a high of 38 percent late on Friday afternoon, dealers said.
They said the heavy fluctuation was due to some mismatches in some banks following the weekly tax payments and the last day of liquidity reports, which caused the rate to soar.
One Japanese bank dealer said the situation seemed to have stabilised in the morning, but operators were still keen to wait for the outcome of Tuesday's tax payments.
Dealers said early central bank injection of some 831 billion rupiah seemed to have helped the market although some carry-forward impact was still being felt.
They said swap rates seemed to have narrowed money market levels which indicated a normalised condition.
Overnight swap was at 0.40/0.45 and tom/next at 0.4/0.42.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 25.22 percent, compared with 11.29 percent on Thursday.
